title: unified-rollouts: proactive-canary-shadow-autorollback-optimizations
author: Ava Patel
body: Summary: This PR refines the proactive canary + shadow autorollback workflow by optimizing probing cadence, improving metric aggregation for short-lived canaries, and adding safety guards to reduce false-positive rollbacks. Motivation: We've observed noisy metric signals for very short canaries (<=30s) and increased rollback churn in regions with higher tail latency variance. This leads to reduced availability and developer trust in automated rollouts. This change reduces unnecessary rollbacks while preserving safety for genuine regressions. What I changed: - Adjust probing cadence: probing intervals are now adaptive based on observed traffic and variance. Short canaries get slightly longer initial probe windows to gather stable metrics. - Improved metric aggregation: introduced percentile-weighted aggregation for latency and composite error scoring that reduces sensitivity to transient tail spikes. - Safety guards: add quorum checks across independent telemetry windows and a minimum sustained degradation window before triggering autorollback. - Observability: add new rollout metrics (rollout.probing.sample_count, rollout.probing.variance_score, rollout.rollback.reason) and dashboards. - E2E/witnessing: extend existing rollout e2e tests to include noisy-latency scenarios and introduce a synthetic-probing harness for simulation. - Backward-compatible config: rollout policy fields are additive and default to previous behavior; customers with pinned policies will see no change unless they opt into the new adaptive probes. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for metric aggregation and quorum logic - [x] Integration tests for rollout controller - [x] E2E test harness updated and passing - [x] Updated docs for rollout policy config and examples - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts added Migration path: No forced migration required. Admins can opt into the new policy via the rollout config: "adaptive_probing: true". For Dedicated/private customers, the new default is off for minor versions; operators can enable via release notes. Related: ENG-18642 (reduce rollback noise), ENG-19011 (rollout telemetry improvements).
commits: feat(rollouts): adaptive probing engine with variance-aware intervals
fix(rollouts): correct percentile-weighted aggregation edge cases
chore(tests): add noisy-latency e2e scenarios for autorollback
docs(rollouts): document adaptive_probing rollout policy and examples
perf(metrics): reduce cardinality in rollout tracing tags
review_comments: Liam Chen: The adaptive probing logic looks solid; one question on the default timers for short canaries - could we expose the initial window as a policy override?
Author (Ava Patel): Yes - added policy field initial_probe_window_ms with a sensible default; documented in rollout_policy.yaml
Sofia Ruiz: Aggregation uses a percentile-weighted mean. Can you add a short note on complexity and worst-case cost?
Author (Ava Patel): Added microbenchmarks and a note in aggregation.rs; overhead is <3% on our staging telemetry workload.
Marcus Lee: Observability metrics are great. Please ensure rollout.rollback.reason tags include model_version and region for downstream analysis.
Author (Ava Patel): Added model_version and region to the rollback.reason tag and updated dashboards.
release_notes: Adaptive probing for canary+shadow autorollback: reduces false-positive rollbacks by variance-aware probing cadence and improved metric aggregation. Opt-in via rollout policy 'adaptive_probing'. Observability additions: rollout.probing.sample_count, rollout.probing.variance_score, rollout.rollback.reason.
merge_outcome: Squash-merged after approvals and CI green. Backported notes provided for Dedicated/private customers.
